title: Q1 2026: reported genre hit counts; supply and hit rates unavailable
scope: Steam releases dated 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-31, sampled from VG Insights on April 2; not indie-only.
methodology: Threshold: at least 1,000 reviews by cutoff. Chris Zukowski manually assigns one genre per qualifying game. Exact counts extracted from the public article's genreData variable, not inferred from chart thickness. Genre supplies are not published; rates remain null.

caveats: Genre counts total 74, but the all-Steam >=1,000-review bucket contains 96. The article does not explain the 22-game discrepancy; do not normalize these rows to 96 or present them as exhaustive.
Canvas fallback text says 63.2% for 0–9 reviews. Its raw counts and runtime formula yield 61.7%; other fallback percentages also disagree. Preserve raw counts and label recalculations.
No same-taxonomy genre-supply denominator or full public game-level cohort was linked or found. Null is unknown, not zero.
Late-March games had far less exposure than January games. Do not compare this early-quarter snapshot directly with mature full-year 2025 hit rates.
Direction compares published Q1 hit counts, not revenue, audience growth or likelihood of success. A zero means no hit in this chart, not zero demand.
Categories are hand-assigned and exclusive; Steam tags overlap. Mixing tagged supply with these hit counts would produce invalid rates.
'Real Steam' and the review threshold are the author's heuristic, not a published Valve algorithm trigger. Review counts do not prove organic acquisition or profitability.
The full-year projection and its 23.7% growth are forecasts. Current SteamDB totals may use different snapshots or definitions.
